reasons: Only 13 of 18 sections were provided, and the main ExperienceJourney component was not reviewed.
Several rules rely on hard-coded identifiers that are easy to break.

terms.meaning: a reusable building block of a React page that combines layout and behaviour
the named settings that are passed into a component from outside
a React helper that stores a computed result and only recalculates it when its inputs change
a browser attribute that stops a section from receiving mouse or keyboard focus
a permanent identifier given to a published paper
a publisher website where research papers are listed
two display styles in this app: calm uses plain-English text, nerd uses technical wording and terminal-style labels

sections.name: File setup, ORIGIN
sections.title: Imports and origin lookup
sections.what: Brings in the shared components and data the journey view needs. The ORIGIN table maps each job id to a matching project origin, so each job can find its own projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple lookup table links each job to its projects. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: A new job must be added to ORIGIN, or it will show no project cards.

sections.name: Win
sections.title: Shape of a floating window
sections.what: Describes what a floating window holds: an id, a title, an optional small meta label, a dark-style flag, and its body content.
sections.why: Gives the role summary and expanded cards one shared window format.
sections.watch_out: Window ids should stay unique, or expanded windows may conflict.

sections.name: Tile
sections.title: Shape of a card
sections.what: Describes one card: its group, title, optional kicker line, preview, image, art, and full body content. The group must be one of the eight named groups.
sections.why: Keeps every card in the same format so the panel can sort and display them.
sections.watch_out: Grouping works by exact name, so a misspelt group name silently drops the card from the grouped view.

sections.name: years
sections.title: Reading years from a period
sections.what: Pulls the start and end years out of a period string such as a date range. A period marked present uses the current year plus a little, and the label shows Now.
sections.why: Likely reason: periods are stored as text, so the years must be read out to build the timeline label. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: The present end uses the current year, so the timeline shifts each year. A period with no year or only one year gives empty or undefined values.

sections.name: Shot
sections.title: Image that hides on failure
sections.what: Shows a grayscale picture that fills its frame. If the picture fails to load, it draws nothing.
sections.why: Avoids showing a broken-image icon on the page.
sections.watch_out: Failed images disappear with no placeholder, so a bad file path is easy to miss. If a card looks empty, check its image path first.

sections.name: roleWindow
sections.title: Role summary window
sections.what: Builds the summary window for one job, showing the company, role, period, location and a description. If there is no description, it shows a note saying details are to be added. The title changes between calm and nerd modes.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is likely the top card that every job view begins with.
sections.watch_out: The company name is cut at the first comma in the title, so a company name with a comma in it will look shorter.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER (part 1)
sections.title: Highlight and project cards
sections.what: Makes one card for each highlight and one for each key project in a job. A project card shows a short description and the places it covered, with full detail on expansion.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is likely to show the main achievements and projects first.
sections.watch_out: Place names come from a lookup. A place id missing from that lookup is dropped without any message.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER (part 2)
sections.title: Industry cards linked to projects
sections.what: Makes one card for each industry in a job. Each card gets a generated art panel listing the role, period, project count and up to three linked projects. Projects are linked by loose text matching on the industry name.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a visitor see which projects belong to each industry. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Matching is based on text, so a project can be linked to the wrong industry or missed entirely.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER (part 3)
sections.title: Tool cards from projects
sections.what: Adds a card for each project whose origin matches the job. The card uses a screenshot when one exists, and shows either calm or nerd text. It links to the project's own page.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is likely to show the tools built during each job.
sections.watch_out: A project whose origin does not match any job will never appear. The project page link is built from the slug, so a changed slug breaks the link.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER: if
sections.title: Paper cards for one role
sections.what: For the role with the id parikshit only, adds a card for each paper. Each card shows a page snapshot, venue, year, details, authors and DOI, and links to the publisher page.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Papers are tied to this one role in the data, and the check is hard-coded.
sections.watch_out: Renaming the parikshit id removes all paper cards with no warning.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER (part 5)
sections.title: Photo and methods cards
sections.what: Adds a photo card for each memory linked to the role, skipping paper images. Photos are numbered in the order of the memories list. If the role has problem statements or methods, it adds one methods card listing them.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Photos give a visual sense of each role, and the methods card explains the approach.
sections.watch_out: Photo titles are numbered by list position, so reordering the memories data renames the photos.

sections.name: tilesFor, GROUP_ORDER (part 6)
sections.title: Link cards and the tile list
sections.what: Adds a link card for each external link, except for the parikshit role, which gets none. The function then returns the full list of cards for the job.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parikshit role's papers already link out to the publisher, so separate link cards would repeat them. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: The exception repeats the parikshit id, so any change of that id must be made in this place as well as the paper rule.

sections.name: Panel (part 1)
sections.title: Job panel layout
sections.what: Draws the selected job: a role summary and a globe map with a place list on the left, and grouped cards on the right. Clicking a card opens it in a larger window. Only the active job draws its contents, and hidden jobs are marked inert.
sections.why: Drawing only the active job keeps the page lighter. The inert marking stops hidden content from being reached by keyboard.
sections.watch_out: The panel is rebuilt when the mode changes, so the text switches between calm and nerd modes immediately.

sections.name: Panel (part 2)
sections.title: Role card contents
sections.what: Fills each role card in the timeline with its optional picture, an industry illustration, a small label line, and a short preview. Each card is a button, so a click opens the full text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cards stay short so many roles fit side by side, while the full detail appears only in the pop-up.
sections.watch_out: The picture and illustration are optional, so a role with neither shows text only. Keep this in mind when adding roles.

sections.name: ExperienceJourney (part 1)
sections.title: Timeline state and sorting
sections.what: Sorts the roles from oldest to newest, then tracks which role is showing, whether the tour is playing, and which role is open in the pop-up. It starts on the newest role and keeps the chosen position inside the list.
sections.why: The sort makes the timeline read forward in time, as the code comment says.
sections.watch_out: The sort uses the start year parsed from each role's period text, so a badly written period can place a role in the wrong order.

sections.name: ExperienceJourney (part 2)
sections.title: Automatic tour and keyboard controls
sections.what: Starts a slow automatic tour the first time the section is at least 45 percent on screen, and pauses it when the section scrolls away. The Escape key closes the pop-up, and the arrow keys move between roles.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tour plays once so visitors see it on arrival, and pauses so it does not run off-screen.
sections.watch_out: When the browser asks for reduced motion, the automatic start is skipped entirely.

sections.name: ExperienceJourney (part 3)
sections.title: Year ruler and step buttons
sections.what: Draws a year ruler with a mark for each role, highlights the current role, and shows previous and next buttons with the current position and year.
sections.why: Lets visitors jump to any role or step through them one at a time, and shows where the current role sits in time.
sections.watch_out: The ruler ends one year after the current year, so the timeline stretches as the calendar moves on.

sections.name: ExperienceJourney (part 4)
sections.title: Sliding role track and pop-up
sections.what: Slides the role panels sideways so the active one is in view, responds to swipes longer than 60 pixels, and opens a full-text pop-up that closes on a background click or the Escape key. A footer line shows the education entry.
sections.why: The slide and swipe let phone visitors move through roles the same way desktop visitors do.
sections.watch_out: The footer education text comes from a separate data file, so edits there appear here without code changes.

summary: Builds the per-job journey view: for each role it creates a summary window, a map of where the work went, and cards grouped into highlights, projects, tools, papers, photos, industries, methods and links.
purpose: Lets a visitor explore one job at a time, moving from the role summary into its projects, papers, photos and links.
why: Likely reason: presents each role as a set of explorable cards rather than a single long text. The code does not state the overall intent. Only the first 13 of 18 sections were provided, so the main component that switches between roles is not reviewed here.
how: 1. The tilesFor function turns one job's data into a list of cards, adding a card for each highlight, key project, industry, tool, paper, photo, method and link. 2. Each card is assigned a group name. 3. The Panel component builds the role window and map for the active job, then arranges the cards in the order given by GROUP_ORDER. 4. Clicking a card opens it in a larger window. 5. Hidden job panels are marked inert, so keyboard focus cannot reach them.
inputs: Job records from the battles data, the projects, papers, memories and asset lookups, place names, and the display mode, which is either calm or nerd. The active flag says which job panel is being shown.
outputs: Rendered job panels with a role summary, a globe map, a place list, and grouped cards that open in larger windows.
risks: Several rules depend on fixed identifiers. The ORIGIN table decides which projects belong to a job, and the paper and link rules depend on the job id parikshit. A new job missing from ORIGIN gets no project cards. Images that fail to load are hidden with no placeholder, so a bad path can look like missing content.
debug: If a job shows few cards, check the job data fields and the ORIGIN entry for that job. If papers or links are missing for parikshit, check the hard-coded id in the paper and link rules. If images are missing, check the asset path. If text does not switch between calm and nerd modes, check the mode value passed to Panel.
